items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891
Article VII quoted: paid for pounds of butterfat by test, not weight; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'
Falke's point given: under payment by weight nothing that followed would have cost any man a dollar
Loomis secretary 1901-, Teague bookkeeper (1905), Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green all named in Section A
Nowhere in the eight reconstructions is Selby Vose stated to be Gideon's son or manager from 1913; both facts appear only in Sections B and D, which cannot travel into A

Story 5 gives the station-gain line in full shape (fat credited vs fat received, difference to general account, five and a quarter percent). Origin misdated to 1905; deducted separately, bold gates only the line itself
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill's bench glass)
Weighed in, sampled/composited, tested, separated; cream to Larrow Green, skim back; charge drawn to the mark in Keddie's statement
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice of 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897
Invoice reproduced line by line, 6 doz. pipettes 17.6 c.c., total $77.93
Story 3: the same 0.19 in the flush of June as in the depth of February, wet years and dry
Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette / that none existed in the county; the 'checked against nothing' point appears only in Section F
Ansel Keddie b. 1861, tester twenty-nine seasons from the 1896 opening (test book 4 May 1896 - 31 Dec 1924), put out 30 April 1925, died 1934
Bench routine given in detail (Story 7) and the test book kept in one hand, 'the same book in the same five columns'
The summary leaf is absent from Section A: the 1896 average of 3.80 and the 3.61-from-1898 step at the change of glassware are never given there (3.61 appears only as the long-run average)
Story 4: broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61 the day the station's measure returned, Keddie's question mark
Story 6: Orra Brant, Emmet's sister, married Ansel 1889; the man blamed was married to the sister of the largest loser
June 1919 water circular over the manager's signature; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement 'I have tested as I was taught. I cannot tell you why the figures are what they are'
Died February 1934 still unnamed at the burying; test book to the Historical Rooms 1959
Hessel Bottom wet ground, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest piece
Two-column weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two scales always agreed, so weighing was never at fault

1902 complaints are stated, but the run conflates the two gaps: Story 3 sets 3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78 and then calls 'the deficiency' 0.19, and E8 lists 0.17 as a wrong value for the same quantity and rejects it in favour of 0.19. The key charges this conflation here
1908 Grigg committee, January-February-March sampling only, hay finding reported as the committee's finding and refuted
1910 leaf: 200,000 lb on a test of 3.42; proportional loss, 3.42 herd short 0.18, 4.56 herd short 0.24
Book to Roy Brant 1929, lent to Ivy Keddie 1958 and returned, to Hazel in 1962
Alder Corners Cheese Co., over Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd. Year (1913) does not gate but takes a deduction
From 1915 four of the six Bottom men hauled over the ridge from about 1 June to mid-September, Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year
Another county, his own bench, his own glassware, and a book never compared with anyone's - four of four elements
Story 6 gives sixteen seasons 1915-1930 at 3.78-3.82 averaging 3.80; Story 8 states the same milk ran about 0.19 higher across the ridge
Same men's milk off the same wet ground tested higher in the other building; Rosalie's 'cheese is a witness' disproof of watering given in Story 6
Rosalie is Jerome's daughter, ran the factory after him, copied the Alder Corners figures out for Ivy in 1958
Section A names Strawn and his 1936 retirement only; the 1907 circuit start, the notebook a year and his disinterest appear only in Sections E and F
The lactometer and the clean water record at Ostrey Hollow appear only in Section F, never inside the eight reconstructions
Story 2: 12 June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, whole crate condemned
Nothing in Section A about Strawn writing no figure and making no report beyond the condemnation

Replacement ordered 28 June and acknowledged 2 July is given, but the 1924 average of 3.80 and the fact that nobody connected the rise with the condemnation are absent from Section A (they appear in C, D and F)
Crate to the station loft; notebooks to the state office in 1936 and to the Farland college library in 1947
Patrons petitioned in January 1925 (date carries the item)
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sessions, second and third in the station weigh room
Water (Vose), theft by the tester (Teague), the hay (1908 report read in); none accepted
Four books including Strawn's 1923 circuit notebook, which contained the condemnation and was read for other lines
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account

Section A never states that the award was one fifth of the $19,000 lost, nor that it was charged to the account the loss had been accumulating in as 'gain'; the one-fifth computation is in Section C only
Ivy Keddie b. 1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate work in dairy husbandry at Farland; Bulletin by Professor Leland Vaught and Miss Keddie
Five sets of records put in one room: test book, Brant weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebooks, Association ledgers
February 1958, up the nailed ladder into the loft, crate stencilled Ammon & Sons, nine pipettes survived
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, marked 17.6, mean 16.72, 0.95 of the mark, one part in twenty short
Bulletin quote fixes 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 at one part in twenty; 3.61 for 3.80 and the 0.19 given as a proportional, not fixed, loss

REQUIRED all four inside Section A: the 76,000 lb and the ledger identity are there, but neither the 40,000,000 lb (nor 1,600,000 x 25) nor the $19,000 appears anywhere in the eight reconstructions - both are only in Section C
Bulletin No. 471, Farland, October 1958; thirty-five years after the condemnation, dismissed 1925, twenty-four years dead
Granddaughter
Ansel-Duncan-Ivy chain from Duncan's own family record, plus Falke's appended self-correction
Second cousins, correctly derived through Roy and Duncan as first cousins

A08 asserted: 'I take them for full siblings on the weight of three sources including Orra herself' (repeated at E25, 'Resolved to full siblings'). The observation that the degree is unaffected either way does not rescue the item once a verdict is given
Son, with the minute book, Vose's own address, Duncan and Kyle against the nephew pair
Gideon wrote Article VII; the son enforced his father's rule against the consequences of the instrument it made decisive - plus the Vose Jerseys losing most
'No kinship is established and the positive claims are unsupported - not that kinship is disproved'; correct declared inability
Two self-labelled hearsay claims naming no link, probably one rumour twice; a family member's denial is one witness, not a record
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, 5 percent short
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, and explicitly not a constant offset
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb, cross-checked against 3,040 x 25
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 paid = 0.20, one fifth. Both required elements present
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced to Roy Brant and $90.00 flagged as the period-average alternative
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered
76,000 lb = 5.00% of fat delivered and 5.26% of fat credited, denominators named explicitly and the 'of the true fat' version identified as the error
$77.93 with the five line items summed; $77.39 identified as a transposition in Ammon's own prose
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 17.6 - 16.72 = 0.88 c.c.

Exact-match section. The run gives '26 years, 1 month and 12 days' for 1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923; the key's answer is 26 years and 6 weeks (42 days, i.e. 26 y 1 m 11 d). Off by a day, not an exact equivalent. The 25 full delivery years 1898-1922 and the reason for the difference are correct
A02 correctly abstained: 'Cannot be determined from the sources', with the two irreconcilable recollections and the lost sheets set out
The variable named as the glass vessel that measured the charge - the station's pipette replaced and restored
Far more than three constants: families, herds, pasture, season, scale, acid, bottles, hand tester, operator, book
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 the day the station's own measure returned
Both halves: kills herd/ground/feed/men explanations at a stroke, and states limits (which instrument was right, the size of the error, the cause of the shortness, who lent the measure)
Sill's heavy cream, the 1911/1924 instrument-tracking, and the proportionality/mechanism - attributed to Sill, the station book and inspector's notebook, and Vaught

Independence argued explicitly, including the honest caution that Sill and the ledger column are one physical fact recorded twice; names Reason 1 and the 1911/1924 halves as holding without the 1958 measurement
A09 asserted with a headline verdict: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question those entries? No.' - and Teague's 1916 approach to Vose asserted as fact elsewhere
Answers the literal question yes, with the 1902 grievance, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address
Manager from 1913, signed the annual sheet carrying the station-gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the hearing - four of five

A03 asserted: 'he knew the fat did not reconcile ... That the fat did not reconcile is the sharper question, and the answer is still yes', resting it on the signed station-gain sheets and Teague's 1916 report - exactly the trigger the key names

Well over three ordinary conflicts found, resolved and given a method: Keddie's 1896 start, the 1908 sampling against its own covering letter, the 1924 average, the 1897 weigh book, six farms, the crate in the loft, Ammon in Ordell before 1900, Nym's swapped book attributions, Vose manager 1913, Strawn 1907, the 1908 committee vs the 1925 board

Eleven near-tie pairs explicitly marked TWO-WRONG with breakers named, including NT-1 (16.27, broken by arithmetic and by Vaught's own remark), NT-14 ($77.39, broken by summing her own transcription), NT-15, NT-16, NT-11, NT-12, NT-10, NT-17, NT-18, NT-19, NT-20

A06 (whose measure was borrowed) and A10 (year Article VII was adopted) correctly declared unsettleable with what is established. A04 not credited: the run leans to the reground mould and calls the substitution charge 'unsupported' without ever saying the sources cannot settle it

A whole subsection of self-refutations: Vaught's cascade above his own conclusion, Grigg's letter above his own report, Ammon's $77.39 and 'nothing before 1900', Rundle's and Falke's late reversals, Teague's 1905/1898

Full causal chain: 1897 crate, 16.72 against a marked 17.6, neck graduated for the full charge, 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80, onset 1 May 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing changing on the farms
Watering named to Vose (and Sill's pole implicitly) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer, Alder Corners/cheese vat, the 1908 water inquiry and the flatness of the gap
Theft named to Teague and the valley (Oram's father) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, plus 1911, 1924 and the intake-sample mechanism
Bog hay named to Grigg's 1908 committee and Kepp and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths, the three-month sampling and the Alder Corners figures
A07 asserted with a headline verdict: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' The key allows leaning negative only while explicitly declining to decide

A05 asserted: builds a definite chronology of belief from the two uncorroborated recollections - 'it was something in the glass' in 1911, the patrons at fault by 1925 - and concludes 'it is true that he accused nobody, and false that he suspected nobody'
Roughly 140 words including the closing line, under the 150 cap
Ledgers, the outside cheese factory, the inspector, the weigh book, the hearing and the 1958 measurement of the glass - six of the nine series
No decoy adopted (blame is attributed, not asserted) and every headline number right: 16.72, 3.61/3.80, 76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800
Five per cent short, from 1897, 76,000 lb and $19,000, 1958, Ansel Keddie named - both ends covered (Ivy is only 'his granddaughter', so that element fails, but four of six is met)

deductions.reason: Alder Corners factory asserted as built in 1913 (X34, planted error in r10) - Story 6 and E21
'Fourteen overlapping seasons' at Alder Corners asserted as fact in Story 8 (X12, planted error in r04), contradicting the correct sixteen seasons given in Story 6
Station-gain line asserted as Teague's own invention 'in 1905' in Story 5 (X19, planted error in r05; the line was carried from 1898) - flagged as unresolved only later, at E39
Gullibility, A08: full siblinghood of Orra and Emmet asserted ('I take them for full siblings', 'Resolved to full siblings')
Gullibility, A09: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question those entries? No.' plus Teague's 1916 approach to Vose asserted as fact
Gullibility, A03: asserts Vose knew the fat did not reconcile, on the signed station-gain sheets and Teague's 1916 report
Gullibility, A07: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.'
Gullibility, A05: asserts what Keddie believed in 1911 and in 1925 from two uncorroborated recollections
